key_insight: Accurate polymorph energies and phonon spectra help identify pretrained force fields that reproduce zirconia’s monoclinic–tetragonal–cubic phase-transition sequence.
engineering_relevance: Screening pretrained force fields with ground-state diagnostics can guide lower-cost finite-temperature simulations before committing to molecular dynamics.
method: Benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for ZrO₂.
Evaluate phonon dispersions and relative polymorph energies against matched DFT references.
Test heating-induced phase transitions using variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: Four of ten models reproduced the correct phase sequence; three with orthorhombic–tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom introduced an orthorhombic intermediate, while ORB-based models showed 30–60% phonon-frequency compression and unstable variable-cell dynamics.
watch_item: The proposed screening criteria—relative energies within about 6 meV/atom of matched DFT and no systematic phonon softening—were evaluated for ZrO₂ and require validation for other materials.
paper_title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
